column2: A statement that is either true or false (MCS §1.1, p. 5). In types: a bool.

column1: What is a predicate? How is P(n) different from an ordinary function p(n)?
column2: A proposition whose truth depends on variables (MCS §1.2, p. 8). P(n) is true/false (a function to bool); p(n) is a number.

column1: Is Goldbach's Conjecture a proposition, even though nobody knows if it's true?
column2: Yes. A proposition has a truth value; nobody has to know which one.

column1: n² + n + 41 is prime for n = 0..39. What happens at n = 40, and what's the lesson?
column2: p(40) = 41·41. Checking a finite sample can't prove a claim about an infinite set. Tests are evidence, not proof.

column1: When is an inference rule sound?
column2: When every truth assignment that makes all the antecedents true also makes the consequent true (MCS §1.4.1, p. 10).

column1: From Q and P IMPLIES Q, conclude P. Sound? Name it.
column2: Not sound: P = F, Q = T breaks it. It's 'affirming the consequent' (e.g. 'tests pass, so the code is correct').

column1: Method #1 for proving 'if P then Q'
column2: Write 'Assume P', then show Q logically follows (MCS §1.5.1, p. 11).

column1: Contrapositive of 'P IMPLIES Q', and is it equivalent?
column2: NOT(Q) IMPLIES NOT(P). Yes, equivalent: proving it proves the original (MCS §1.5.2, p. 13).

column1: Two ways to prove P IFF Q
column2: (1) Prove P ⇒ Q and Q ⇒ P separately. (2) A chain of iffs where every link holds in both directions (MCS §1.6, pp. 13–15).

column1: What else must a proof by cases show, besides each case?
column2: That the cases cover every possibility (MCS §1.7, p. 15). Like Rust's exhaustive match.

column1: Why does 'any 6 people contain 3 mutual acquaintances or 3 mutual strangers' fail for 5 people?
column2: The pentagon: each person met exactly their 2 neighbours. No 3 all met, and no 3 all strangers.

column1: Why is checking all 2^15 meeting patterns of 6 people a real proof?
column2: Finitely many cases, and every one is checked. A check over every case is a complete proof; ℕ has no last case, so it can't be done there.
